name: Attention Dissolving into Space, a Wall, or a Worthy Vessel
previous_label: Virabhadrasana I — Warrior I (asana framing, retired 2026-10)

dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24, sequential, one verse per dhāraṇā for 1–16)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: īdṛśena krameṇaiva yatra kutrāpi cintanā | śūnye kuḍye pare pātre svayaṃ līnā varapradā ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, checked against Singh, Wallis's concordance and Pradīpaka
dharana.rendering: In the same graded way, wherever attention rests, whether on empty space, on a wall, or on a worthy vessel, it dissolves there by itself and grants the boon.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer; not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: 'pare pātre' is read differently: Singh 'some excellent person' (glossed as a pure-minded, competent pupil), Bäumer 'a worthy disciple', Chaudhri 'a great person', Silburn 'receptacle suprême', Wallis 'a perfect vessel'. Singh and S. P. Singh & Maheshvarananda tie 'in this same way' back to the twelve stations of verse 30.
dharana.technique_name: Attention Dissolving into Space, a Wall, or a Worthy Vessel

checked_against: GRETIL, Pradīpaka and Wallis: verse text matches the technique
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dharana number, verified directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against at least one independent edition. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: Y7 (Wallis groups verses 24–27 as one technique)
numbering_variants.popular_lists: Old notes say some popular lists put an all-directions space visualisation at dharana 10; that claim could not be traced to a named edition and is unverified.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 33 does not prescribe a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: a single support for attention: empty space, a blank wall, or a worthy vessel
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is one line of attention from the practitioner to a single plain support, ending where attention dissolves into it.
geometry.svg_hint: a single line of attention ending on a blank rectangle (wall) or open space, fading at the end
geometry.honesty: Redefined in 2026-10: geometry now records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Dissolve into the support
reaction.summary: School metaphor: diffuse attention gathers on one plain support and then dissolves into it, without claiming any biochemical change.

breath.cue: Natural breath, about four in and four out if counting helps. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Face one plain support: open sky, a blank wall, or a worthy presence
orientation.gravity: Body supported so that nothing distracts from the support
orientation.gaze: Soft, steady, unblinking only as long as it is comfortable
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: One plain support (space, wall, or worthy vessel), held until attention dissolves into it

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: In the same graded way, wherever attention rests, whether on empty space, on a wall, or on a worthy vessel, it dissolves there by itself and grants the boon.
adiyogi.method_summary: Rest a soft gaze on empty sky or a blank wall, keep attention there without chasing thoughts, and let it dissolve into the support. Optional variant: briefly rest attention on the presence of someone you hold as worthy, then return to the breath. Contemplative focus only, not ritual or force.

honesty.disclosure: Door 010 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 10 (verse 33) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type stays school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's. The original honesty text is kept below in honesty.legacy, with retired posture names redacted; the verbatim text is at previous_file.
flags: Door index = Jaideva Singh dharana number: Door 010 is dharana 10, verse 33. Other editions number differently (see dharana.numbering_variants).
The seat, breath counts, reaction metaphor, attention-map drawing and beat scripts are school devices, not part of the verse.
The English is a school paraphrase, not a quotation from any translator.
No medical claims. Reaction names are metaphors, not biochemistry.
Reframed from the earlier posture framing on 2026-10-06; awaiting guardian re-review. The previous review covered the posture framing only.

legacy.disclosure: This [retired posture]↔method link is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device, not ancient canon. Door index 010 is paired with VBT method/dharana 010 by school map.
legacy.notes: Numbering note: many practice commentaries present Verse ~33 (void / wall / worthy person) as skill/dharana 10; some popular lists place an all-directions space visualization at dharana 10. This draft follows the void/wall/worthy-person lane as VBT dharana 010 and discloses the school pairing.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. Blink whenever needed; do not strain the eyes by staring. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

legacy_notes.open_seat_alternate: If the flat back foot or hip rotation agitates the back knee or hip, use [retired posture] (back heel lifted, hips freer) or shorten the stance. Do not force the pelvis square.
legacy_notes.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only for knees, hips, low back, and neck (especially if looking up). Not medical advice; regress depth or exit when needed.
legacy_notes.status: Posture-specific cautions, kept for traceability; they no longer apply because this door teaches no posture.

beats.title: Name the door
beats.script: This is Door 010: attention dissolving into space, a wall, or a worthy vessel. Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 10, verse 33.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit where you can see open sky or a plain wall. The map is one line of attention to one plain support.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Body supported. Soft, steady gaze on the support. Blink when you need to.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath, four in, four out. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Keep attention on the support. Let thoughts pass without following. Let attention melt into what it rests on.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: scattered attention is absorbed by one support. Metaphor only.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 33: wherever attention rests, on space, a wall or a worthy vessel, it dissolves by itself and grants the boon. Stay with the field; do not chase thoughts.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Look away from the support. Take in the whole room. Move on when ready.
